Project Charter Template

                     Course Team Project Charter
                 CE/CS/SE 3354 Software Engineering

1. Project Summary

Project Title    UTD Fitness

Project Sponsor  CS/CE/SE 3354.006 Dr. Barbara Maweu

Project Manager  Rafael Amador

Start Date       09/10/2026

Target End Date  11/10/2026

Charter Date / Version 09/10/2026 - V#1

2. Purpose / Business Case

Explain why this project exists and what problem it solves. In a course context, this is your
project motivation.

Problem Statement

Students' health usually takes a toll when school is taking up much of their time. The solution is
a health-tracking app that integrates with the school's infrastructure, such as the UREC center,
club activities, and sports events. Overall, this app will help students track their steps to reach
their health goals, measure their water intake, reduce the use of electric vehicles around campus,
and solve the calorie-tracking problem of manually inputting ingredients by taking pictures to
calculate the macronutrients with the use of a trained AI.

Business / Academic Justification

This problem is relevant to today's student life because about 40% of American adults and 20%
of youth are affected by obesity (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention). The general
culprit is the lack of knowledge about what program to follow and the overwhelming amount of
conflicting information, making it hard for people to know which habits are good and which are
bad to follow. Apart from personal health, this app would improve and promote a healthy student
life outside of classes, encourage healthy competition, and support intramural sports and school
 club sports. Overall health promotes a strong mind, and a strong mind can promote better
performance in school. Without this app students could miss out on having a much more vibrant
and healthier lifestyle for student life and future life.

3. Project Objectives

List specific, measurable objectives (align with your anticipated functional requirements).

The objective of this application is to promote healthy habits that extend beyond their student
career. There are a few ways that we will implement this habit amongst students. One of the
methods we will encourage students to live a healthier lifestyle is by creating a point based
system that rewards students for completing certain actions. One way of getting points is by
swiping your card at the UREC center or completing tasks that encourage activity. There will be
ways to log food for caloric intake as well as goal setting to help keep students on track. A water
tracker will also be implemented to ensure students can be hydrated throughout the day. There
will also be a map showing the different and closest areas to refill their water. These features
within the app will help promote healthy daily habits for students to continue in their future.

4. Scope

In Scope

     Calorie intake tracking via manual input or an AI that can calculate calories based on a
         camera image.

     Track water intake by taking note of the volume of the user's water bottle and calculating
         water intake based on the number of refills.

     Ability to connect to smart devices like smart watches.
     Store and display a user profile consisting of user-entered public information.
     Make connections through adding other users as friends.
     Heartrate tracker compatibility with smart devices.

Out of Scope

     Exclude push notifications to encourage user discipline.
     No web application as it will mainly be a mobile application.
     Exclude tracking specific gym exercises (how many sets on what exercise, machine

         weight, etc.)
     No tracking for medications.
     No sleep tracker.
     No subscriptions or ads.

5. Stakeholders & Project Team
 Identify everyone with a stake in the project and each team member's role.

Name             Role                                   Responsibility

[Member Full Name] [Role, e.g., Backend Developer] [One-sentence responsibility]

Rafael Amador    Architecture Engineer                  Handling work flow between
                                                        members, and making sure
                                                        progress is going in the right
                                                        direction.

Joseph Babuchna  Frontend Developer                     Creating and coding the part of
                                                        the app that the user will see so it
                                                        is easy to use and not confusing
                                                        to learn.

Ameen Chougle    Backend Developer                      Handling student data and
                                                        shipping to backend

Richard Jang     Quality Assurance (QA)                 QA ensures everything is
                                                        functional and follows
                                                        requirements.

Sean Chang       Design/UI                              Creating the design of the app
                                                        and how the users interact

Arnav Kumar      Database Engineer                      Designs and manages the
                                                        database structure, making sure
                                                        user data is stored, organized, and
                                                        retrieved correctly.

Aryansh Chaturvedi Requirements Engineer                Keeps track of project
                                                        requirements and documentation,
                                                        making sure the team's work
                                                        matches the project
                                                        specifications.

6. Deliverables & Milestones

High-level timeline of what will be produced and when.

Milestone / Deliverable                   Owner                             Target Date
Project Charter submitted                 Rafael Amador                     9/11/2026
   Deliverable #1: Requirements & diagrams      Rafael Amador    9/25/2026
  finalized                                                     10/9/2026
                                                                10/23/2026
  Deliverable #1: Architecture & design complete Rafael Amador  10/30/2026

  Deliverable #2: Scheduling, Prototype        Rafael Amador
  implementation / Test Plan complete

  Deliverable #2: Final report & presentation  Rafael Amador
  complete

7. Assumptions & Constraints

Assumptions

  Many assumptions are taken into account for this project. Primarily, we are assuming that

students will be honorable in their tracking of food and water, as no honor system can

contractually be put in place. While their steps can be linked directly to smart devices and their

phone itself, we will not be checking as to whether they tried to make those numbers up

themselves. Another assumption that we are making is that all students do have a phone and

carry it on their person at all times. As we will not be expanding to a web-app, this tracker will

only exist on students' phones. This is fine because most, if not all, university students do own a

phone and carry it all the time.

  As per the budget and how the overall funding of this project will go, we are also

assuming that we will be getting sponsorship either from the university, or from an external

source. We will not be implementing a profit model into the application. Finally, we are

assuming for the leaderboard function that more than one person will eventually use this

application.

Constraints

  Many constraints are in place that could cause problems during development. One

constraint is that since we do not have a profit model, our timeline could be affected in the

anticipation of funds. Additionally, we are also planning to not have any microtransactions on

this application, such as a membership model, which could also affect funding.

  Furthermore, our overall structure of the app could also be affected due to the fact that we

are not expanding to a web-app. This could lead to low user count in the future, also being

affected by us only keeping gym tracking/swiping to the UTD UREC center and not external

gyms and home gyms.

8. Risks
 Identify what could threaten the project's success and how you'll respond.

  Risk                             Likelihood     Impact                    Mitigation
  [Describe risk]
                                   [Low/Med/High [Low/Med/High [Mitigation plan]

                                   ]              ]

  Not enough users                 High           High                      Advertisement of
                                                                            the app/
                                                                            Cooperation with
                                                                            clubs/
                                                                            Incentives

  Not enough funds to host the app Med            High                      Reaching out to
                                                                            sponsors

  User over-exertion               Low            Med                       Warnings of the

                                                                            app

  Too many users, which will crash Low            High                      Have scalability
  the app                                                                   on the overall
                                                                            infrastructure

9. Budget & Resource Estimate

Budget: $67,800 + $23180 per year

  Development: $67,800

    Labor Costs:

                      $20 per hour per person, for seven people, $140 per hour.

                      $67,200 for three months of development (assuming 40 hour work weeks.

    Tools and resources:

                      Github Enterprise, Figma, Claude Code

                      $200 per month - $600 for three months of development

  Recurring costs / Maintenance: $23180 per year

    Hosting the app on the app store and google play store: $180 per year

    Database for the app: $600 per year
                 Servers for the app: $2400 per year

                Maintenance of app: $20,000 per year

10. Success Criteria

Define what "done" and "successful" look like for this project.

              The app can accurately track and Display:
                       Steps taken
                       Calorie and water intake
                       Profiles and leaderboard statistics

              No outages of the app
                       App has an uptime of at least 99.9%

              At least � of UTD is on the app
                       ~7500 users

11. Approval

All Team members sign-off indicates agreement on scope, roles, and objectives before work
begins.

  Each Team Member Name Role                                     Signature / Date
                                                                 Ameen Chougle 9/10/26
  Ameen Chougle       Backend Developer

  Sean Chang          Design/UI                                  Sean Chang 9/10/26

  Richard Jang        QA                                         Richard Jang 9/10/26

  Rafael Amador       Architect                                  Rafael Amador 9/10/26

  Joseph Babuchna     Frontend developer                         Joseph Babuchna 9/10/26

  Aryansh Chaturvedi  DataBase Engineer                          Aryansh Chaturvedi 9/13/26

  Arnav Kumar         Requirements Engineer                      Arnav Kumar 9/13/26

  complete

7. Assumptions & Constraints

Assumptions

  Many assumptions are taken into account for this project. Primarily, we are assuming that

students will be honorable in their tracking of food and water, as no honor system can

contractually be put in place. While their steps can be linked directly to smart devices and their

phone itself, we will not be checking as to whether they tried to make those numbers up

themselves. Another assumption that we are making is that all students do have a phone and

carry it on their person at all times. As we will not be expanding to a web-app, this tracker will

only exist on students' phones. This is fine because most, if not all, university students do own a

phone and carry it all the time.

  As per the budget and how the overall funding of this project will go, we are also

assuming that we will be getting sponsorship either from the university, or from an external

source. We will not be implementing a profit model into the application. Finally, we are

assuming for the leaderboard function that more than one person will eventually use this

application.

Constraints

  Many constraints are in place that could cause problems during development. One

constraint is that since we do not have a profit model, our timeline could be affected in the

anticipation of funds. Additionally, we are also planning to not have any microtransactions on

this application, such as a membership model, which could also affect funding.

  Furthermore, our overall structure of the app could also be affected due to the fact that we

are not expanding to a web-app. This could lead to low user count in the future, also being

affected by us only keeping gym tracking/swiping to the UTD UREC center and not external

# CometFit server configuration.
# Default profile = PostgreSQL (the "Encrypted Database" of Deliverable 1 §5.3.2), run via docker-compose.
# Profile "h2" = embedded file database for laptops without Docker (ASSUMPTIONS A-2).
server:
  port: ${PORT:8080}

spring:
  application:
    name: cometfit-server
  datasource:
    url: ${DB_URL:jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/cometfit}
    username: ${DB_USER:cometfit}
    password: ${DB_PASSWORD:cometfit}
  jpa:
    open-in-view: false
    hibernate:
      ddl-auto: validate
    properties:
      hibernate.jdbc.time_zone: UTC
  flyway:
    enabled: true
  servlet:
    multipart:
      max-file-size: 10MB
      max-request-size: 10MB

management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health

cometfit:
  # Local day boundary for daily summaries (A-9)
  zone: ${COMETFIT_ZONE:America/Chicago}
  # Session lifetime in hours (A-6)
  session-hours: ${COMETFIT_SESSION_HOURS:12}
  # Base64 AES-256 key used to encrypt sensitive user fields at rest (NFR Security, A-5).
  # The default is a DEVELOPMENT key only. Set COMETFIT_DATA_KEY in any shared environment.
  data-key: ${COMETFIT_DATA_KEY:Q29tZXRGaXQtZGV2LW9ubHkta2V5LWNoYW5nZS1tZSE=}
  # Shared secret that external systems (UREC card reader, monitoring service) present (A-12).
  integration-key: ${COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY:dev-integration-key}
  # Monitoring service stub interval (SD-4 "loop every interval", MonitoringService.checkIntervalSec)
  monitoring:
    check-interval-sec: ${COMETFIT_MONITOR_INTERVAL_SEC:30}
    stub-enabled: ${COMETFIT_MONITOR_STUB:true}
  # Seed demo accounts (developer + two students) with fixed TOTP secrets (A-14). Demo only.
  seed-demo: ${COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO:true}
  # Allowed browser origins for the web build of the mobile client
  cors-origins: ${COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS:http://localhost:8081,http://localhost:19006}

---
spring:
  config:
    activate:
      on-profile: h2
  datasource:
    url: ${DB_URL:jdbc:h2:file:./data/cometfit;MODE=PostgreSQL;DATABASE_TO_LOWER=TRUE;DEFAULT_NULL_ORDERING=HIGH}
    username: ${DB_USER:sa}
    password: ${DB_PASSWORD:}

# CometFit local stack: PostgreSQL = the "Encrypted Database" of Deliverable 1 §5.3.2 (A-2).
# Start:  docker compose up -d db        (from the app/ folder)
# The server can also run in the container: docker compose up -d --build
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: cometfit
      POSTGRES_USER: cometfit
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-cometfit}
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - cometfit-db:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U cometfit -d cometfit"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  server:
    build: ./server
    profiles: ["full"]
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      DB_URL: jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/cometfit
      DB_USER: cometfit
      DB_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-cometfit}
      COMETFIT_DATA_KEY: ${COMETFIT_DATA_KEY:-Q29tZXRGaXQtZGV2LW9ubHkta2V5LWNoYW5nZS1tZSE=}
      COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY: ${COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY:-dev-integration-key}
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"

volumes:
  cometfit-db:

This is an Expo/React Native mobile application. Prioritize mobile-first patterns, performance, and cross-platform compatibility.

## Expo has changed — do not trust your training data

Expo ships breaking changes every SDK release. APIs you remember are likely renamed, moved, or removed. Before writing any code that touches an Expo, EAS, or React Native API:

1. Read the major version of the `expo` package in `package.json`.
2. Fetch the matching versioned docs: `https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v<major>.0.0/`
3. For anything else, fetch https://docs.expo.dev/llms.txt — an index of all Expo docs with corrections to common LLM misconceptions. Follow its links to the specific page you need; never answer from memory.

## Commands

Use `bunx` instead of `npx` if the project uses bun (`bun.lock` present).

```bash
npx expo install <package>  # ALWAYS use instead of npm/yarn/pnpm/bun add — resolves SDK-compatible versions
npx expo start              # start the dev server
npx expo lint               # lint
npx tsc --noEmit            # typecheck
npx expo-doctor             # diagnose dependency and config issues
npx expo install --fix      # fix incompatible package versions
```

Run lint and typecheck before declaring any task done.

## Navigation & Routing

- Use **Expo Router** for all navigation. Routes live in `src/app/` — every file there is a screen, `_layout.tsx` files define navigators. Keep non-route code (components, hooks, utils) outside `src/app/`.
- Import `Link`, `router`, and `useLocalSearchParams` from `expo-router`.
- Docs: https://docs.expo.dev/router/introduction.md

## Building with EAS

Use EAS to build, sign, and submit the app in the cloud (`eas build`, `eas submit`) and to ship over-the-air updates (`eas update`) — no local Xcode or Android Studio required. Run EAS CLI as `bunx eas-cli <command>` in Bun projects, or `npx eas-cli@latest <command>` otherwise; substitute that for bare `eas` in docs examples.
Docs: https://docs.expo.dev/eas/index.md

## Rules

- If `ios/` and `android/` directories do not exist, they are generated (Continuous Native Generation). Never create or edit them by hand — configure native behavior in `app.json` and config plugins.
- Expo Go only includes its bundled native modules. After adding a library with native code, the app needs a development build: `npx expo run:ios|android` locally, or `eas build --profile development`.
- Prefer recommended Expo modules over third-party libraries, and check your available skills before adding dependencies. Docs: https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/index.md

# CometFit — local setup and demo guide

CometFit (SE 3354 Team 9) is a student health-tracking app: meals and water (UC-1), activity and UREC visits (UC-2),
friends' progress (UC-3), and developer monitoring and control (UC-4). It was built only from the team's Proposal and
Deliverable 1. `../TRACEABILITY.md` maps every requirement to code and tests. `../ASSUMPTIONS.md` lists every gap
that had to be filled.

```
app/
├── server/            Spring Boot REST server: API gateway, auth gateway, Nutrition / Activity / Social / Admin services
├── client/            Expo (React Native) mobile app — also runs in a web browser for the demo
├── tools/             totp.mjs (prints sign-in codes), smoke.mjs (end-to-end HTTP check)
└── docker-compose.yml PostgreSQL database (and optionally the server)
```

The architecture follows Deliverable 1 §5.3 (client-server): the mobile client talks to one REST API, and every call
goes through the auth gateway (password + TOTP sessions, permissions list) and the module (feature-flag) check before
it reaches a service. Outside systems (AI food recognition, UTD Dining menus, smart devices, the UREC card reader,
the monitoring service and the alert channel) are **stubs**. They are labelled `*** STUB ***` in the code and listed at
the end of this file.

---

## 1. Install prerequisites

| Tool | Version used | Check with |
|---|---|---|
| Java JDK | 21 or newer (built with 23) | `java -version` |
| Maven | 3.9+ | `mvn -v` |
| Node.js + npm | Node 22+ | `node -v` |
| Docker Desktop | optional, for PostgreSQL | `docker version` |

Without Docker, use the embedded H2 database (step 3, option B).

## 2. Install dependencies

```bash
# server (downloads the Maven dependencies)
cd app/server
mvn -DskipTests package

# client
cd ../client
npm install
```

## 3. Configure environment variables

Every variable has a development default, so **nothing needs to be set for a local demo**. For anything shared, set
at least `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`, `DB_PASSWORD` and `COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`.

### Server (`app/server`)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | `8080` | HTTP port |
| `DB_URL` | `jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/cometfit` (H2 file `./data/cometfit` with the `h2` profile) | JDBC URL |
| `DB_USER` / `DB_PASSWORD` | `cometfit` / `cometfit` | Database login |
| `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY` | development key | Base64 32-byte AES key that encrypts emails and TOTP secrets at rest. Generate one: `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64'))"`. **Changing it makes existing accounts unreadable.** |
| `COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY` | `dev-integration-key` | Shared secret that the UREC card reader and the external monitor send in the `X-Integration-Key` header |
| `COMETFIT_ZONE` | `America/Chicago` | Time zone that defines "today" for daily totals |
| `COMETFIT_SESSION_HOURS` | `12` | Session lifetime |
| `COMETFIT_MONITOR_INTERVAL_SEC` | `30` | Health-check interval of the monitoring stub |
| `COMETFIT_MONITOR_STUB` | `true` | Run the built-in monitoring-service stub |
| `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO` | `true` | Create the demo accounts below on start-up |
| `COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS` | `http://localhost:8081,http://localhost:19006` | Browser origins allowed to call the API |

### Client (`app/client`)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` | `http://localhost:8080` (`http://10.0.2.2:8080` on the Android emulator) | Server base URL |

To set variables: in bash, `export NAME=value`. In PowerShell, `$env:NAME = "value"`. You can also put client
variables in `app/client/.env` (this file is git-ignored).

## 4. Run the project locally

### Start the database and server

**Option A — PostgreSQL in Docker (default profile)**

```bash
cd app
docker compose up -d db          # PostgreSQL 16 on localhost:5432
cd server
mvn spring-boot:run
```

**Option B — no Docker (embedded H2 file database)**

```bash
cd app/server
mvn spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=h2
```

Either way, Flyway creates the schema on first start. The server is ready when
<http://localhost:8080/actuator/health> shows `{"status":"UP"}`. The H2 data is stored in `app/server/data/`;
delete that folder to start over.

*(Optional: run everything in containers with `docker compose --profile full up -d --build`.)*

### Start the client

```bash
cd app/client
npm run web            # opens http://localhost:8081 in the browser
```

For a phone-like view in the browser, use the dev tools' device toolbar. On a real phone, run `npx expo start` and
open the app in Expo Go. Set `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` to your laptop's LAN address, for example
`http://192.168.1.20:8080`.

### Sign in

| Username | Password | TOTP secret | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alice` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITALICE234` | Student |
| `bob` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITBOBBY567` | Student |
| `dev` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITDEVADMIN` | Developer (admin dashboard) |

Every sign-in needs the current 6-digit code. Get it from any authenticator app (add the secret), or from:

```bash
node app/tools/totp.mjs COMETFITALICE234
```

New students can register from the sign-in screen. The app then shows their own TOTP secret once.

## 5. Run the tests

```bash
cd app/server && mvn test        # 38 API/unit tests on H2, one test class per use case (Uc1..Uc4) + security
cd app/client && npm test        # client unit tests (Node test runner)
cd app/client && npm run typecheck

# End-to-end over real HTTP against a running server (uses the demo accounts):
node app/tools/smoke.mjs http://localhost:8080
```

## 6. Demo script (about 5 minutes)

1. **UC-1** — Sign in as `alice`. On **Log**, tap *+1 refill*, then log a meal manually. Switch to *Dining menu* →
   *Dining Hall* → *Add* an item. Switch to *Photo (AI)* and pick any image, edit the estimate, then *Confirm & save*.
   **Today** shows calories, macros, water progress and the low-water message.
2. **Safety** — in **Profile → Daily goals**, enter 800 kcal or 6000 ml and watch the warnings appear.
3. **UC-2** — **Activity** → *Connect smart device* → *Allow* (simulated health prompt) → *Sync now*. Then
   *Simulate UREC card swipe*, which earns +10 points and appears in the visit history.
4. **UC-3** — **Friends** → search `bob` → *Profile* → *Add friend*. In a second browser window (or a private
   window), sign in as `bob` and *Accept*. As `alice`, turn sharing on under *What my friends can see*. As `bob`,
   open alice's *Stats* and the leaderboard.
5. **UC-4** — Sign in as `dev`. The dashboard shows uptime % and per-service status. Click *Simulate outage* on a
   service to see a downtime alert and an incident, then end it. *Disable* "Friends & Leaderboard" and switch to
   bob's window: the Friends tab shows the maintenance notice while the other tabs keep working. *Re-enable* it.

## 7. Stubs (external systems from the spec)

| External actor in the spec | Interface | Stub implementation |
|---|---|---|
| AI Food Recognition Service (UC-1) | `services/AIFoodService` | `stubs/FakeAIFoodService` — deterministic estimate from the image hash |
| UTD Dining menu data (UC-1, FR-8) | `services/UtdDiningFeed` | `stubs/StubUtdDiningFeed` — fixed sample menu for "Dining Hall" and "Campus Store" |
| Smart Device pairing (UC-2) | `services/SmartDeviceGateway` | `stubs/FakeSmartDeviceGateway` — always pairs, except device ids starting with `FAIL` |
| Smart Device readings + health permission (UC-2) | client `src/smartDevice.ts` `SmartDeviceAdapter` | `FakeSmartDevice` — simulated steps / heart rate |
| UREC Card Reader (UC-2) | `POST /api/activity/visits` with the integration key | `stubs/FakeUrecCardReader` — the "Simulate UREC card swipe" button |
| Monitoring Service (UC-4) | `POST /api/admin/health-check` with the integration key | `stubs/MonitoringAgentStub` — timer inside the server |
| Downtime alert channel (UC-4) | `services/AlertNotifier` | `stubs/LoggingAlertNotifier` — logs the alert and shows it on the dashboard |
| A real outage (demo only) | — | `stubs/OutageSimulator` — the "Simulate outage" button |

## 8. REST API overview

All endpoints except register, login and health need `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

| Area | Endpoints |
|---|---|
| Auth | `POST /api/auth/register`, `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/logout`, `GET /api/auth/me` |
| Profile (FR-3) | `GET/PUT /api/profile`, `PUT /api/profile/password`, `PUT /api/profile/goals` |
| Nutrition (UC-1) | `POST /api/nutrition/meals/photo`, `GET /api/nutrition/menu/locations`, `GET /api/nutrition/menu?location=`, `POST/GET /api/nutrition/meals`, `POST/GET /api/nutrition/water`, `GET /api/nutrition/summary` |
| Activity (UC-2) | `POST/GET /api/activity/devices`, `DELETE /api/activity/devices/{id}`, `POST /api/activity/steps`, `GET /api/activity/records`, `POST /api/activity/visits` (reader), `GET /api/activity/visits`, `POST /api/activity/stub-reader/swipe` |
| Social (UC-3) | `GET /api/social/users/search?q=`, `GET /api/social/users/{id}`, `POST/GET /api/social/requests`, `POST /api/social/requests/{id}/accept\|decline`, `GET /api/social/friends`, `DELETE /api/social/friends/{id}`, `GET/PUT /api/social/consent`, `GET /api/social/friends/{id}/stats`, `GET /api/social/leaderboard` |
| Modules (FR-5) | `GET /api/modules`, `GET /api/modules/{id}` |
| Admin (UC-4) | `GET /api/admin/access`, `GET /api/admin/uptime?hours=`, `POST /api/admin/uptime/check-now`, `GET /api/admin/alerts`, `GET /api/admin/modules`, `POST /api/admin/modules/{id}/disable\|enable`, `POST /api/admin/health-check` (monitor), `POST /api/admin/stub/outage` |

When a module is disabled, its endpoints answer `503 {"code":"MODULE_DISABLED"}` and the app shows a maintenance
notice.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Cannot reach the CometFit server"** in the app: the server isn't running, or `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` is wrong.
- **Login fails with a correct password:** the 6-digit code is wrong or expired, or the laptop clock is off.
- **Port 8080 already in use:** start the server with `PORT=8081`-style overrides (`mvn spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.arguments=--server.port=8090`) and point `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` at it.
- **CORS error in the browser:** add the page's origin to `COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS`.
- **"Could not decrypt field":** `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY` changed after the accounts were created. Restore the old key or reset the database.

| Auth | `POST /api/auth/register`, `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/logout`, `GET /api/auth/me` |
| Profile (FR-3) | `GET/PUT /api/profile`, `PUT /api/profile/password`, `PUT /api/profile/goals` |
| Nutrition (UC-1) | `POST /api/nutrition/meals/photo`, `GET /api/nutrition/menu/locations`, `GET /api/nutrition/menu?location=`, `POST/GET /api/nutrition/meals`, `POST/GET /api/nutrition/water`, `GET /api/nutrition/summary` |
| Activity (UC-2) | `POST/GET /api/activity/devices`, `DELETE /api/activity/devices/{id}`, `POST /api/activity/steps`, `GET /api/activity/records`, `POST /api/activity/visits` (reader), `GET /api/activity/visits`, `POST /api/activity/stub-reader/swipe` |
| Social (UC-3) | `GET /api/social/users/search?q=`, `GET /api/social/users/{id}`, `POST/GET /api/social/requests`, `POST /api/social/requests/{id}/accept\|decline`, `GET /api/social/friends`, `DELETE /api/social/friends/{id}`, `GET/PUT /api/social/consent`, `GET /api/social/friends/{id}/stats`, `GET /api/social/leaderboard` |
| Modules (FR-5) | `GET /api/modules`, `GET /api/modules/{id}` |
| Admin (UC-4) | `GET /api/admin/access`, `GET /api/admin/uptime?hours=`, `POST /api/admin/uptime/check-now`, `GET /api/admin/alerts`, `GET /api/admin/modules`, `POST /api/admin/modules/{id}/disable\|enable`, `POST /api/admin/health-check` (monitor), `POST /api/admin/stub/outage` |

When a module is disabled, its endpoints answer `503 {"code":"MODULE_DISABLED"}` and the app shows a maintenance
notice.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Cannot reach the CometFit server"** in the app: the server isn't running, or `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` is wrong.
- **Login fails with a correct password:** the 6-digit code is wrong or expired, or the laptop clock is off.
- **Port 8080 already in use:** start the server with `PORT=8081`-style overrides (`mvn spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.arguments=--server.port=8090`) and point `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` at it.
- **CORS error in the browser:** add the page's origin to `COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS`.
- **"Could not decrypt field":** `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY` changed after the accounts were created. Restore the old key or reset the database.

# Assumptions

Every gap that had to be filled because `spec/` (Project Proposal = "Prop", Deliverable 1 = "D1") is silent or
ambiguous. Code comments reference these IDs.

A-n | what was missing | choice made | related spec section
---|---|---|---
A-1 | How the "Server" box (API gateway, auth gateway, 4 services, encrypted DB) is deployed; load balancing / telemetry details | One Spring Boot process with one package per box: `gateway` (API gateway + module routing), `security` (auth gateway), `controllers`+`services` (Social / Activity / Nutrition / Admin), PostgreSQL. Load balancing is not built for a laptop demo; telemetry = health checks + uptime records (FR-1). | D1 §5.3.1, §5.3.2, §5.3.3
A-2 | Which database product; Docker Engine not running on the build machine | PostgreSQL 16 (docker-compose) is the default. An `h2` Spring profile (embedded file DB, PostgreSQL mode) lets the app run and be tested without Docker. The same Flyway schema is used for both. | D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"; Prop §9 "Database for the app"
A-3 | How accounts are created (every use case includes "Log In" but there is no sign-up use case) | Students self-register (username, password, email, display name) and get a TOTP secret to add to an authenticator app. Developer accounts are created by seed/config only. | D1 Fig 4.3 "Log In (Password + TOTP)"; NFR Security
A-4 | Credential rules | Username 3–30 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_.]`, unique (case-insensitive); password ≥ 8 chars; email must look like an address. | NFR Security
A-5 | What "all user data will be encrypted" means concretely | Passwords: BCrypt hash. Email and TOTP secret: AES-256-GCM field encryption (key from `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`). Other tables (meals, steps, …) rely on database/disk-level encryption in a real deployment, because the app must sum and query them. TLS is expected from the deployment's reverse proxy; the local demo uses plain HTTP. | NFR Security, NFR Legislative-Security; D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"
A-6 | Login flow detail and session lifetime | One login call carries username + password + 6-digit TOTP code; a Session (random 256-bit token, Bearer header) is created only if both factors pass, and lasts 12 h. `AuthService.authenticate` therefore takes the TOTP code as a third argument. TOTP = RFC 6238, SHA-1, 30 s, ±1 step. | D1 §5.2 AuthService, Session; NFR Security
A-7 | Default goals for a new student | 2000 kcal, 2000 ml water, 10 000 steps, 500 ml bottle. Students can change them. | D1 §5.2 Student (calorieGoal, waterGoalMl, stepGoal)
A-8 | Where the water-bottle size lives (Prop: "volume of the user's water bottle … number of refills"; SD-1 "log water (bottle size / refill)"; class diagram has no field) | Added `bottleSizeMl` to Student (set in Profile → Goals). The app logs a refill as `saveWaterEntry(bottleSizeMl)`, plus half bottle or a custom amount. | Prop §4; D1 SD-1
A-9 | What "daily" means (time zone of the day boundary) | Configurable `COMETFIT_ZONE`, default America/Chicago (D1 cites the Texas Data Privacy and Security Act, so the users are in Texas). | D1 UC-1 "View Daily Summary & Goals"
A-10 | Thresholds for an "unsafe goal" | Warn when calorie goal < 1200 or > 4000 kcal, water goal < 1000 or > 4000 ml, step goal > 30 000 (Prop risk "User over-exertion → Warnings of the app"). The goal is still saved; the app only warns (NFR says "allow a warning"). | D1 NFR Safety; Prop §8
A-11 | Which "portions of the app" can be shut down | Three modules, each mapped to an API prefix: NUTRITION (`/api/nutrition`), ACTIVITY (`/api/activity`), SOCIAL (`/api/social`). Login, profile and admin cannot be disabled. A disabled module answers 503 `MODULE_DISABLED`, and the client shows a maintenance notice on those tabs. | FR-5; D1 UC-4, SD-4 ("disable module (e.g. Friends)")
A-12 | How external systems (UREC card reader, monitoring service) authenticate | Shared secret in header `X-Integration-Key` (`COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`). Card readers must also be registered in `urec_card_readers`; seed reader `UREC-FRONT-1` at "UREC front desk". | D1 §5.3.2 External Systems; SD-2, SD-4; NFR Security
A-13 | Names and contents of the "backend permissions list" | Students implicitly hold `nutrition.use`, `activity.use`, `social.use`, `profile.use`. Developers hold an explicit list; the seeded developer has `admin.uptime.view`, `admin.modules.manage`, `profile.use`. Developers do not get student features. | D1 NFR Security; §5.2 Developer.permissions; UC-4 "Authorize Admin (Permissions + TOTP)"
A-14 | Data for a recorded demo | When `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO=true` (default), seed developer `dev` and students `alice` and `bob`, password `CometFit123!`, with fixed, published TOTP secrets. Demo only; turn it off anywhere real. | PROMPT (demoable in a video)
A-15 | Behaviour of the "AI Food Recognition Service" | Stub: picks 1–2 entries from a fixed placeholder table, deterministically from the image's SHA-256. The estimate is shown for review and is saved only after the student confirms or edits it. The photo itself is not stored. | D1 UC-1 "Log Meal by Photo"; SD-1; Prop §2
A-16 | UTD Dining menu content and locations | Stub feed with two locations, "Dining Hall" and "Campus Store" (from FR-8's rationale "campus stores and dining hall"), and 5 placeholder items each. Each `getMenu` call refreshes items from the feed into `dining_items` (keyed by the feed's item id), so meal entries can reference them. | FR-8; D1 UC-1 "Maintain Dining Menu & Macros"; §5.2 DiningItem
A-17 | Meaning of `steps` in a pushed ActivityRecord | Steps counted since the previous sync (an increment). Daily steps = sum of the day's records. Limits per push: steps 0–100 000, heart rate 20–250 bpm. | D1 SD-2 "pushSteps(steps, heartRate, timestamp)"; §5.2 ActivityRecord
A-18 | Default data-sharing consent | All four `share*` flags default to false; nothing is visible to friends until the student turns it on. | D1 NFR Legislative-Privacy; §5.2 ConsentSettings
A-19 | When water intake is "too low" (FR-6 verification) | Any time today's total is below the student's water goal, the daily summary includes a "water intake is low" message. Reaching the goal shows a "goal reached" message instead. | FR-6 RTM verification method (D1 §4.4)
A-20 | Point values and limits | UREC visit: 10 points, awarded only for the first visit of each day (later swipes are still recorded). Reaching the daily step goal: 5 points, once per day. Points are never deducted. | Prop §3 "point based system"; D1 UC-2 "Earn Points", SD-2 `awardPoints(studentId, VISIT)`
A-21 | What the leaderboard ranks and who appears on it | Rank = point balance (ties share a rank), among the student and their friends. Points come only from visits and steps, so a friend appears (and their points show in their stats) only if they share visits or steps. | D1 UC-3 "View Leaderboard"; NFR Legislative-Privacy; Prop §7 leaderboard
A-22 | What `isPublic` controls | Non-friends viewing a private profile see only the username, not the display name or member-since date. Search by username always works, so friend requests are still possible. | D1 §5.2 User.isPublic; FR-3; Prop §4 "user-entered public information"
A-23 | How the friend is "notified of request" (Prop excludes push notifications) | In-app only: the request appears in the receiver's *Friend requests* list. | D1 SD-3 "notify of request"; Prop §4 Out of Scope
A-24 | Delivery channel for downtime alerts and when to send one | Stub `LoggingAlertNotifier`: logs a WARN line and keeps the last 50 alerts for the admin dashboard. An alert fires when a service goes down (first down check) and again when it recovers, not on every check. | D1 UC-4 "Raise Downtime Alert"; SD-4 alt [service down]
A-25 | Which "servers" are monitored, how often, how long records are kept | 7 components named after the §5.3.2 boxes (api-gateway, auth-gateway, nutrition-service, activity-service, social-service, admin-service, database), each with a real probe. Checks run every 30 s (configurable); uptime % is the share of successful checks over the chosen window (default 24 h). Records are kept 30 days. | FR-1; D1 SD-4 loop [every interval]; §5.2 MonitoringService.checkIntervalSec
A-26 | Client technology, given "mobile app only, no web application" (Prop §4, §7) vs. the requirement that the demo runs in a browser | Cross-platform Expo / React Native app (NFR Development: "native or cross-platform mobile app"). The same app is run through react-native-web for the laptop demo; this is a way to run the mobile client, not a separate web product. The phone-sized layout is kept. | Prop §4 Out of Scope; D1 NFR Operational, NFR Development; PROMPT
A-27 | What the UREC card carries to identify the student | The card reader sends the student's CometFit user id as `studentId` (the class diagram has no separate card-number field). | D1 SD-2 `recordVisit(studentId, time)`; §5.2 UrecCardReader.sendSwipe(studentId)
A-28 | Smart-device link rules | A health-data permission must be granted before linking (UC-2 «include» Grant Health Permissions). A device can be LINKED to only one student at a time. Unlinking keeps history. In the browser, the OS permission prompt and the wearable are simulated (client `FakeSmartDevice`). Optional automatic sync runs every 60 s while the Activity screen is open. | D1 UC-2, SD-2; NFR Interoperability
A-29 | Editing or deleting logged meals, water or visits | Not provided; the spec only describes logging and viewing. | D1 UC-1, UC-2
A-30 | Range of friend statistics | A friend's stats show today's calories, water and steps (with goals), UREC visits in the last 7 days, point balance, and leaderboard rank, each only if consented. | D1 UC-3 "View Friend's Statistics"; SD-3

# Assumptions

Every gap that had to be filled because `spec/` (Project Proposal = "Prop", Deliverable 1 = "D1") is silent or
ambiguous. Code comments reference these IDs.

A-n | what was missing | choice made | related spec section
---|---|---|---
A-1 | How the "Server" box (API gateway, auth gateway, 4 services, encrypted DB) is deployed; load balancing / telemetry details | One Spring Boot process with one package per box: `gateway` (API gateway + module routing), `security` (auth gateway), `controllers`+`services` (Social / Activity / Nutrition / Admin), PostgreSQL. Load balancing is not built for a laptop demo; telemetry = health checks + uptime records (FR-1). | D1 §5.3.1, §5.3.2, §5.3.3
A-2 | Which database product; Docker Engine not running on the build machine | PostgreSQL 16 (docker-compose) is the default. An `h2` Spring profile (embedded file DB, PostgreSQL mode) lets the app run and be tested without Docker. The same Flyway schema is used for both. | D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"; Prop §9 "Database for the app"
A-3 | How accounts are created (every use case includes "Log In" but there is no sign-up use case) | Students self-register (username, password, email, display name) and get a TOTP secret to add to an authenticator app. Developer accounts are created by seed/config only. | D1 Fig 4.3 "Log In (Password + TOTP)"; NFR Security
A-4 | Credential rules | Username 3–30 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_.]`, unique (case-insensitive); password ≥ 8 chars; email must look like an address. | NFR Security
A-5 | What "all user data will be encrypted" means concretely | Passwords: BCrypt hash. Email and TOTP secret: AES-256-GCM field encryption (key from `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`). Other tables (meals, steps, …) rely on database/disk-level encryption in a real deployment, because the app must sum and query them. TLS is expected from the deployment's reverse proxy; the local demo uses plain HTTP. | NFR Security, NFR Legislative-Security; D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"
A-6 | Login flow detail and session lifetime | One login call carries username + password + 6-digit TOTP code; a Session (random 256-bit token, Bearer header) is created only if both factors pass, and lasts 12 h. `AuthService.authenticate` therefore takes the TOTP code as a third argument. TOTP = RFC 6238, SHA-1, 30 s, ±1 step. | D1 §5.2 AuthService, Session; NFR Security
A-7 | Default goals for a new student | 2000 kcal, 2000 ml water, 10 000 steps, 500 ml bottle. Students can change them. | D1 §5.2 Student (calorieGoal, waterGoalMl, stepGoal)
A-8 | Where the water-bottle size lives (Prop: "volume of the user's water bottle … number of refills"; SD-1 "log water (bottle size / refill)"; class diagram has no field) | Added `bottleSizeMl` to Student (set in Profile → Goals). The app logs a refill as `saveWaterEntry(bottleSizeMl)`, plus half bottle or a custom amount. | Prop §4; D1 SD-1
A-9 | What "daily" means (time zone of the day boundary) | Configurable `COMETFIT_ZONE`, default America/Chicago (D1 cites the Texas Data Privacy and Security Act, so the users are in Texas). | D1 UC-1 "View Daily Summary & Goals"
A-10 | Thresholds for an "unsafe goal" | Warn when calorie goal < 1200 or > 4000 kcal, water goal < 1000 or > 4000 ml, step goal > 30 000 (Prop risk "User over-exertion → Warnings of the app"). The goal is still saved; the app only warns (NFR says "allow a warning"). | D1 NFR Safety; Prop §8
A-11 | Which "portions of the app" can be shut down | Three modules, each mapped to an API prefix: NUTRITION (`/api/nutrition`), ACTIVITY (`/api/activity`), SOCIAL (`/api/social`). Login, profile and admin cannot be disabled. A disabled module answers 503 `MODULE_DISABLED`, and the client shows a maintenance notice on those tabs. | FR-5; D1 UC-4, SD-4 ("disable module (e.g. Friends)")
A-12 | How external systems (UREC card reader, monitoring service) authenticate | Shared secret in header `X-Integration-Key` (`COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`). Card readers must also be registered in `urec_card_readers`; seed reader `UREC-FRONT-1` at "UREC front desk". | D1 §5.3.2 External Systems; SD-2, SD-4; NFR Security
A-13 | Names and contents of the "backend permissions list" | Students implicitly hold `nutrition.use`, `activity.use`, `social.use`, `profile.use`. Developers hold an explicit list; the seeded developer has `admin.uptime.view`, `admin.modules.manage`, `profile.use`. Developers do not get student features. | D1 NFR Security; §5.2 Developer.permissions; UC-4 "Authorize Admin (Permissions + TOTP)"
A-14 | Data for a recorded demo | When `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO=true` (default), seed developer `dev` and students `alice` and `bob`, password `CometFit123!`, with fixed, published TOTP secrets. Demo only; turn it off anywhere real. | PROMPT (demoable in a video)
A-15 | Behaviour of the "AI Food Recognition Service" | Stub: picks 1–2 entries from a fixed placeholder table, deterministically from the image's SHA-256. The estimate is shown for review and is saved only after the student confirms or edits it. The photo itself is not stored. | D1 UC-1 "Log Meal by Photo"; SD-1; Prop §2
A-16 | UTD Dining menu content and locations | Stub feed with two locations, "Dining Hall" and "Campus Store" (from FR-8's rationale "campus stores and dining hall"), and 5 placeholder items each. Each `getMenu` call refreshes items from the feed into `dining_items` (keyed by the feed's item id), so meal entries can reference them. | FR-8; D1 UC-1 "Maintain Dining Menu & Macros"; §5.2 DiningItem
A-17 | Meaning of `steps` in a pushed ActivityRecord | Steps counted since the previous sync (an increment). Daily steps = sum of the day's records. Limits per push: steps 0–100 000, heart rate 20–250 bpm. | D1 SD-2 "pushSteps(steps, heartRate, timestamp)"; §5.2 ActivityRecord
A-18 | Default data-sharing consent | All four `share*` flags default to false; nothing is visible to friends until the student turns it on. | D1 NFR Legislative-Privacy; §5.2 ConsentSettings
A-19 | When water intake is "too low" (FR-6 verification) | Any time today's total is below the student's water goal, the daily summary includes a "water intake is low" message. Reaching the goal shows a "goal reached" message instead. | FR-6 RTM verification method (D1 §4.4)
A-20 | Point values and limits | UREC visit: 10 points, awarded only for the first visit of each day (later swipes are still recorded). Reaching the daily step goal: 5 points, once per day. Points are never deducted. | Prop §3 "point based system"; D1 UC-2 "Earn Points", SD-2 `awardPoints(studentId, VISIT)`
A-21 | What the leaderboard ranks and who appears on it | Rank = point balance (ties share a rank), among the student and their friends. Points come only from visits and steps, so a friend appears (and their points show in their stats) only if they share visits or steps. | D1 UC-3 "View Leaderboard"; NFR Legislative-Privacy; Prop §7 leaderboard
A-22 | What `isPublic` controls | Non-friends viewing a private profile see only the username, not the display name or member-since date. Search by username always works, so friend requests are still possible. | D1 §5.2 User.isPublic; FR-3; Prop §4 "user-entered public information"
A-23 | How the friend is "notified of request" (Prop excludes push notifications) | In-app only: the request appears in the receiver's *Friend requests* list. | D1 SD-3 "notify of request"; Prop §4 Out of Scope
A-24 | Delivery channel for downtime alerts and when to send one | Stub `LoggingAlertNotifier`: logs a WARN line and keeps the last 50 alerts for the admin dashboard. An alert fires when a service goes down (first down check) and again when it recovers, not on every check. | D1 UC-4 "Raise Downtime Alert"; SD-4 alt [service down]
A-25 | Which "servers" are monitored, how often, how long records are kept | 7 components named after the §5.3.2 boxes (api-gateway, auth-gateway, nutrition-service, activity-service, social-service, admin-service, database), each with a real probe. Checks run every 30 s (configurable); uptime % is the share of successful checks over the chosen window (default 24 h). Records are kept 30 days. | FR-1; D1 SD-4 loop [every interval]; §5.2 MonitoringService.checkIntervalSec
A-26 | Client technology, given "mobile app only, no web application" (Prop §4, §7) vs. the requirement that the demo runs in a browser | Cross-platform Expo / React Native app (NFR Development: "native or cross-platform mobile app"). The same app is run through react-native-web for the laptop demo; this is a way to run the mobile client, not a separate web product. The phone-sized layout is kept. | Prop §4 Out of Scope; D1 NFR Operational, NFR Development; PROMPT
A-27 | What the UREC card carries to identify the student | The card reader sends the student's CometFit user id as `studentId` (the class diagram has no separate card-number field). | D1 SD-2 `recordVisit(studentId, time)`; §5.2 UrecCardReader.sendSwipe(studentId)
A-28 | Smart-device link rules | A health-data permission must be granted before linking (UC-2 «include» Grant Health Permissions). A device can be LINKED to only one student at a time. Unlinking keeps history. In the browser, the OS permission prompt and the wearable are simulated (client `FakeSmartDevice`). Optional automatic sync runs every 60 s while the Activity screen is open. | D1 UC-2, SD-2; NFR Interoperability
A-29 | Editing or deleting logged meals, water or visits | Not provided; the spec only describes logging and viewing. | D1 UC-1, UC-2
A-30 | Range of friend statistics | A friend's stats show today's calories, water and steps (with goals), UREC visits in the last 7 days, point balance, and leaderboard rank, each only if consented. | D1 UC-3 "View Friend's Statistics"; SD-3
A-31 | Brute-force protection and rate limiting | Not implemented (out of scope for the course prototype). The login error message is the same for every failure, so usernames can't be probed. | D1 NFR Security
A-32 | Visual design (Figma designs are not in `spec/`) | Simple neutral card-based layout with a bottom tab bar (Today, Log, Activity, Friends, Profile) and a separate admin dashboard for developers. | D1 NFR Development ("Figma for design"); NFR Usability

+A-22 | What `isPublic` controls | Non-friends viewing a private profile see only the username, not the display name or member-since date. Search by username always works, so friend requests are still possible. | D1 §5.2 User.isPublic; FR-3; Prop §4 "user-entered public information"

+A-23 | How the friend is "notified of request" (Prop excludes push notifications) | In-app only: the request appears in the receiver's *Friend requests* list. | D1 SD-3 "notify of request"; Prop §4 Out of Scope

+A-24 | Delivery channel for downtime alerts and when to send one | Stub `LoggingAlertNotifier`: logs a WARN line and keeps the last 50 alerts for the admin dashboard. An alert fires when a service goes down (first down check) and again when it recovers, not on every check. | D1 UC-4 "Raise Downtime Alert"; SD-4 alt [service down]

+A-25 | Which "servers" are monitored, how often, how long records are kept | 7 components named after the §5.3.2 boxes (api-gateway, auth-gateway, nutrition-service, activity-service, social-service, admin-service, database), each with a real probe. Checks run every 30 s (configurable); uptime % is the share of successful checks over the chosen window (default 24 h). Records are kept 30 days. | FR-1; D1 SD-4 loop [every interval]; §5.2 MonitoringService.checkIntervalSec

+A-26 | Client technology, given "mobile app only, no web application" (Prop §4, §7) vs. the requirement that the demo runs in a browser | Cross-platform Expo / React Native app (NFR Development: "native or cross-platform mobile app"). The same app is run through react-native-web for the laptop demo; this is a way to run the mobile client, not a separate web product. The phone-sized layout is kept. | Prop §4 Out of Scope; D1 NFR Operational, NFR Development; PROMPT

+A-27 | What the UREC card carries to identify the student | The card reader sends the student's CometFit user id as `studentId` (the class diagram has no separate card-number field). | D1 SD-2 `recordVisit(studentId, time)`; §5.2 UrecCardReader.sendSwipe(studentId)

+A-28 | Smart-device link rules | A health-data permission must be granted before linking (UC-2 «include» Grant Health Permissions). A device can be LINKED to only one student at a time. Unlinking keeps history. In the browser, the OS permission prompt and the wearable are simulated (client `FakeSmartDevice`). Optional automatic sync runs every 60 s while the Activity screen is open. | D1 UC-2, SD-2; NFR Interoperability
+A-29 | Editing or deleting logged meals, water or visits | Not provided; the spec only describes logging and viewing. | D1 UC-1, UC-2

+A-30 | Range of friend statistics | A friend's stats show today's calories, water and steps (with goals), UREC visits in the last 7 days, point balance, and leaderboard rank, each only if consented. | D1 UC-3 "View Friend's Statistics"; SD-3

+A-31 | Brute-force protection and rate limiting | Not implemented (out of scope for the course prototype). The login error message is the same for every failure, so usernames can't be probed. | D1 NFR Security

+A-32 | Visual design (Figma designs are not in `spec/`) | Simple neutral card-based layout with a bottom tab bar (Today, Log, Activity, Friends, Profile) and a separate admin dashboard for developers. | D1 NFR Development ("Figma for design"); NFR Usability

content.text:
CometFit is built: a Spring Boot server, an Expo (React Native) client that also runs in a browser, tests, and the docs. UC-1 to UC-4 and FR-1 to FR-8 are all implemented, and the test runs below passed. Two things were not verified: the PostgreSQL setup and how the screens actually look in a browser (details under "Not verified").

**What was built**
- **Server (`app/server`)** follows the class diagram (§5.2): one class per diagram class, with the same method names (`submitMealPhoto`, `linkDevice`, `filterByConsent`, `disableModule`, …). The flows follow SD-1 to SD-4, and the request path follows the architecture diagram (§5.3): API gateway, then the auth gateway (password + TOTP, permissions list), then the four services and the database.
- **Database:** PostgreSQL via `docker-compose.yml`, with an embedded H2 option so it runs without Docker.
- **Client (`app/client`)** has five tabs (Today, Log, Activity, Friends, Profile) and a separate admin dashboard for developers. A tab whose module a developer has switched off shows a maintenance notice; the other tabs keep working.
- **Stubs:** every outside system in the spec is an interface plus a fake labelled `*** STUB ***`: AI food recognition, UTD Dining menus, the smart device, the UREC card reader, the monitoring service and the alert channel.

**Test results**
- **Server:** 38/38 pass. There is one test class per use case, and the tests follow the verification methods in the spec's traceability matrix (§4.4).
- **Client:** 7/7 unit tests pass, the typecheck is clean, and the web build bundles.
- **End-to-end:** `app/tools/smoke.mjs` walks all four use cases over real HTTP with the demo accounts: 23/23 checks pass, and the browser client's cross-origin calls are accepted.

**Not verified**
- **PostgreSQL:** never run, because Docker Engine wasn't running. The same schema was checked on H2 in PostgreSQL mode.
- **The client in a real browser:** I had no browser automation, so how the screens actually look hasn't been checked.

**Needs your action**
1. **Two leftover server processes** from my smoke tests are still listening on ports 8098 and 8099. Stopping the Maven task didn't stop its Java process, and killing processes needed an approval I couldn't get. To stop them in PowerShell:
   `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 8098,8099 | % { Stop-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess }`
2. **Expo template files:** the template created `app/client/AGENTS.md`, which tells agents to fetch docs from the web, and `app/client/.claude/settings.json`, which enables an Expo plugin. I wasn't allowed to delete them, so I neutralized `AGENTS.md` and git-ignored both. Please delete them, along with the untracked template `LICENSE`.

**Decisions you may want to check** (all 32 are in `ASSUMPTIONS.md`)
- The proposal says "no web application". I treated the browser build as a way of running the mobile app for the demo, not a separate web product (A-26).
- Points: 10 for the first UREC visit each day, 5 for reaching the daily step goal (A-20).
- The leaderboard ranks friends by points and only shows friends who share their visits or steps (A-21).
- Nothing is shared with friends until the student turns it on (A-18).
- Demo accounts `alice`, `bob` and `dev` are seeded with fixed, published TOTP secrets. Turn this off anywhere real (A-14).

There are 13 commits, one per use case for the backend and for the client, plus foundation, tests and docs; nothing was pushed. `app/README.md` has the setup, environment variables, run steps and a 5-minute demo script. `TRACEABILITY.md` maps every FR, use case, non-functional requirement and diagram to its code and tests, and `BUILD_LOG.md` records each step and failure.
